reviews.comment:
If you are purely taking this class for the required life science credit, there are definitely easier classes to take out there. However, if you have some interest in weather/meteorology going into the class, then you will love his lectures!

No homework other than a review before the test, which helps you study anyway, and allows test corrections.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ryan is a fantastic professor. Immediately, you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches and wants the best for all his students. Attendance is mandatory, but I never found it difficult to attend class; I genuinely enjoyed his lectures. Would definitely recommend him!

I liked Ryan a lot super passionate about the subject. Exam-free response was harshly graded I honestly am not 100% sure where I went wrong but I also didn't ask. Homework takes like an hour a week, and it's not super difficult to eek out an A. Would take again.

Ryan North knows stuff about climate change, but when it comes to exams they are tough. For the free response portion get ready to answer based on what his free response his not yours. There are iClicker questions and homeworks that can be lengthy. I would avoid taking this class with Ryan, but everyone else would be fine for this class.
This professor has ruined weather for me. I studied so hard for the tests, but he is so unreasonable when it comes to grading. DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Not the worst class overall, but was overly harsh with the exam free response. You could write an entire paragraph with on-topic, well reasoned points, but since it didn't fit into a narrow mold of acceptable answers, you would get ZERO credit for the question. Office hours were inconclusive. Presented personal opinions mixed in with the facts.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ryan North grades horribly, probably the worst I have ever experienced. His tests have free response that are graded based on his answer, even if one word among 2 sentences is different, he counts the entire thing wrong, no partial credit. In the homeworks, if you even miss the smallest thing, you get a zero, no partial credit. DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!

Passionate about teaching the material but grades excessively hard on the tests. Free responses on the tests were out of 6 points but rarely gave any grade other than a 0 or 6, no in between. He gives no indication on why the free responses are incorrect other than a +0. Overall a very passionate teacher but a very tough grader for a 200 class.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Grading is ridiculous. HW is participation, but if you accidentally skip part of a question, it's a flat ZERO. On exams, multiple choice Qs are misleading, and the free response are difficult to get full points because he has high standards. It doesn't matter if your answer is technically correct, if it's not exactly what he was looking for, ZERO.

He's an associate professor who's still getting into a rhythm of grading for what he wants and doesn't properly outline expectations or correct issues. Also the textbook is unnecessary waste of 40 dollars, I'd recommend if your outside of the meteorology program to try an easier science credit. Expect to watch about an hour of videos and take notes

Ryan was someone who believes that exams are based on his free response not our responses. I failed both the first and second exam, and I studied for 6 hours over a week. This is a 200 level class, and I am doing a lot better in a 300 and 400 level class. I would steer clear of taking this class with Ryan, but if Judy is teaching it take the class.

Ryan is looking for a specific answers on free response questions. If you don't write down exactly what he's looking for, you will lose most or all your points. Some of my classmates dropped as much as 2 letter grades after an exam. On homework, be sure to answer every single question and write in complete sentences, otherwise you will lose points.

Not an easy A. It's evident that he is very passionate about this subject in his lectures. His lectures can feel a little long sometimes, requiring you to take a ton of notes. iClicker quizzes each class, with ~30 seconds to answer them, which can be pretty stressful. Exams were tough. Allows corrections though. Final exam was somehow the easiest.

If you're looking for an easy class to take to fufill your life sciences credit do not take this class. There's weekly homework assignments that take a long time to complete and the exams are actually kind of hard. He offers test corrections but those also take a really long time. Attendance is mandatory
First time teaching Atmo 210. Will give you 0 p

Professor Ryan was by far my favorite professor of the semester. His lectures are very well taught, and the topics he speaks of will relate directly to the exams. There were a lot of concepts entirely new to me, but he made them much easier to understand. GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS, they're extremely helpful for exams. He's super caring and funny too!

Unless you are going into meteorology do NOT take this class. For an elective class, it is so in-depth and difficult. Entire grade is based on three tests and one final. The tests are so hard. And they are locked. Gives no reviews for tests. Attendance is taken for a grade. Lectures have SO much content. You have to take SO MANY NOTES.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. North is extremely passionate about the weather, and that passion is translated right into the class and makes everyone want to learn more about the mysteries of the weather! Great story teller! Easy grader! Participation matters! Beware if you cheat he will catch you!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Ryan is super kind and very nice to talk to. Attendance is mandatory through iClicker and he does provide a few extra credit opportunities aswell as chances to correct exams. The exams are pretty hard but attending office hours helps a lot. Exams are mainly memorization so if you review the slideshow you should be good. Overall, a fun class!

Prof. North was engaging. Attendance was mandatory and class participation counts towards your grade. No late work accepted. The first test is in person and the remainder are either in person or online. I learned a lot in this class. If you prepare for the test, you will do well.

Prof. North is a good lecturer, but the exams are a little tricky and require some solid preparation beforehand. Prof. North is accessible and easy to talk to if you have questions, and he does make the lectures engaging. Most of the grade in the class does come from the exams though.
